rb-0001.title: Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal arithmetic
rb-0001.description: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing money utilities (to_money, round_money, ZERO) rather than raw Decimal operations.
rb-0001.content: Inspect ledgerly/money.py and sibling functions like line_total/invoice_total to match rounding and normalization conventions. Wrap unit prices with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round the final result with round_money.

rb-0002.title: Guard division by zero with the domain's zero constant
rb-0002.description: For weighted-average or ratio computations, check the denominator (total quantity) before dividing and return the project's ZERO constant.
rb-0002.content: Compute total_quantity first; if it equals 0 (empty invoice or zero-quantity lines), return ZERO instead of raising ZeroDivisionError. This satisfies the 'no lines means zero' requirement cleanly.

rb-0003.title: Read the existing test file before implementing
rb-0003.description: Locating and reading the relevant test file (tests/test_average_unit_price.py) alongside models.py and money.py clarified expected types and behavior before writing code.
rb-0003.content: Before editing, cat the target module, its models, its money helpers, and any test file matching the feature name. This reveals signatures, Decimal usage, and edge cases, enabling a first-attempt pass.

rb-0004.title: Reject bool as int for integer validation
rb-0004.description: Python's bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True; explicitly exclude bool when validating positive integers.
rb-0004.content: When validating that a value is a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0`. Without the bool guard, True/False would silently pass as 1/0.

rb-0005.title: Normalize money inputs before sign checks
rb-0005.description: Convert unit_price via the project's to_money helper before comparing against ZERO, so strings/Decimals are handled consistently.
rb-0005.content: Run raw price inputs through the existing money conversion helper (e.g. to_money) first, then compare the normalized Decimal to ZERO for the negative check. This accepts flexible input types while keeping validation correct.

rb-0006.title: Read existing modules to match error conventions
rb-0006.description: Before implementing, inspect errors.py and sibling modules to reuse the project's BillingError codes and helper functions.
rb-0006.content: Explore the repo's error class and existing functions first; reuse established error codes (e.g. invalid_state, invalid_quantity, negative_amount) and helpers rather than inventing new ones. This keeps behavior consistent with hidden tests.

rb-0007.title: Reuse existing timezone-normalization helpers
rb-0007.description: When implementing datetime logic, look for and reuse the repo's existing normalization utility (e.g. ensure_utc) rather than handling tzinfo manually.
rb-0007.content: Search the codebase for helpers like ensure_utc/utcnow before writing datetime code; applying them to both inputs keeps comparisons consistent and matches project conventions.

rb-0008.title: Compute periodic events with floor division on timedelta
rb-0008.description: For 'first occurrence strictly after t' with fixed period from a start, use (t-start)//period then bump if the result is <= t.
rb-0008.content: Compute n = (after - start) // length, renewal = start + n*length, and add one length if renewal <= after. Handle after < start separately by returning start + length so the start itself is never returned.

rb-0009.title: Verify boundary and pre-start edge cases explicitly
rb-0009.description: After passing tests, run quick manual checks for exact-boundary, before-start, and timezone cases to confirm strict-inequality semantics.
rb-0009.content: Write a short python -c script exercising after == start, after == a renewal instant, and after < start; this catches off-by-one errors in 'strictly after' logic that the single provided test may miss.

rb-0010.title: Check idempotency key before any state validation
rb-0010.description: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit trail first and return the stored result before validating payment state or amounts.
rb-0010.content: Team convention requires every balance-changing operation to accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`. Scan `audit.events(<event>)` for a matching key and return the original result (including the stored record) without re-applying. Do this before state checks so retries succeed even after the payment's status has changed.

rb-0011.title: Enforce approval thresholds for large refunds
rb-0011.description: Refunds above 500.00 require a second approver via keyword-only `approved_by=None`, raising BillingError("approval_required") when missing.
rb-0011.content: Finance policy FIN-2026-03: amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise `BillingError("approval_required")` if `approved_by` is falsy. Keep the parameter keyword-only with a default so existing callers keep working, and record `approved_by` in the audit entry.

rb-0012.title: Mirror sibling module conventions when implementing a stub
rb-0012.description: Before writing a new function, read sibling modules (payments, audit, clock, money, errors) to reuse their helpers and error style.
rb-0012.content: The accepted implementation reused `to_money`/`round_money`/`ZERO` from money, `ensure_utc` from clock, `BillingError` from errors, and `audit.record` for the audit trail. Matching existing conventions (rounding, error codes, audit event naming) is what made the diff pass hidden tests.

rb-0013.title: Reuse existing money helpers for currency math
rb-0013.description: When implementing monetary functions, delegate to the repo's existing to_money/round_money helpers rather than raw float arithmetic.
rb-0013.content: Search sibling modules (invoice.py, adjustments.py) for established money utilities and error types before writing new code. Using to_money/round_money and BillingError kept the implementation consistent with the codebase and passed hidden tests on the first try.

rb-0014.title: Validate numeric inputs via Decimal(str(x)) with explicit bool rejection
rb-0014.description: Convert user-supplied rates through Decimal(str(value)) and reject bools, catching InvalidOperation/ValueError to raise the domain error.
rb-0014.content: Booleans are ints in Python, so check isinstance(x, bool) first. Wrapping Decimal(str(x)) in try/except (InvalidOperation, ValueError) handles strings, None, and other junk uniformly, then range-check the Decimal before computing.

rb-0015.title: Read the existing test file for the target function before implementing
rb-0015.description: Locate and read tests referencing the unimplemented function to infer expected return types and error behavior.
rb-0015.content: Grepping for the function name revealed tests/test_tax.py asserting add_tax(Decimal('100.00'), 8) == 108, confirming Decimal-based return values. Checking tests and sibling modules first avoids guessing at conventions.

rb-0016.title: Honor team-convention review comments over literal issue signatures
rb-0016.description: When a review comment states a team convention (e.g., every money-moving operation must accept keyword-only idempotency_key=None), apply it even if the issue text omits it.
rb-0016.content: Review comments labeled [team convention] are binding requirements, not distractors. Add the optional keyword-only parameter so existing callers still work, and implement the described behavior (check-first, return original result, include key in audit entry).

rb-0017.title: Check idempotency key before validating state
rb-0017.description: For idempotent operations, look up prior audit entries by key and return the original result before any state validation or mutation.
rb-0017.content: Iterate audit.events(<event_type>) for a matching idempotency_key and return the stored record immediately. Only after that check should you validate payment.status and raise BillingError('invalid_state', ...). This prevents duplicate side effects and makes retries safe.

rb-0018.title: Follow sibling module conventions for state, time, and audit
rb-0018.description: Match existing patterns in the codebase (ensure_utc for timestamps, BillingError('invalid_state', ...) for wrong state, audit.record with event name and fields).
rb-0018.content: Before implementing, read sibling modules like invoice.py and payments.py to copy conventions: use ensure_utc(at) for stored times, raise BillingError('invalid_state', f'payment {payment.id} is {payment.status}') for invalid transitions, and call audit.record with a descriptive event name plus relevant fields including idempotency_key.

rb-0019.title: Match existing error codes and money helpers before implementing
rb-0019.description: Grep sibling modules for validation patterns and reuse the project's established error codes and money utilities rather than inventing new ones.
rb-0019.content: Before writing a new function, grep for existing patterns like `BillingError(` and `ZERO` across the package. Reusing the exact error code (e.g. `non_positive_amount`) and helpers (`to_money`, `round_money`, `ZERO`) from a sibling module like payments.py keeps behavior consistent and satisfies hidden tests.

rb-0020.title: Use Decimal constants for monetary rates and fixed fees
rb-0020.description: Define percentage rates and fixed fees as module-level Decimal constants, never floats, to avoid rounding drift.
rb-0020.content: Declare `RATE = Decimal("0.029")` and `FIXED = Decimal("0.30")` at module level and compute `round_money(amount * RATE + FIXED)`. Floats are rejected by the project's `to_money`, so all monetary math must stay in Decimal.

rb-0021.title: Read the stub and its tests before implementing
rb-0021.description: When a target file already exists as a stub, read it plus related tests and helpers first to learn the expected signature and conventions.
rb-0021.content: The issue said 'new module' but fees.py already existed as a NotImplementedError stub. Always cat the target file, its test file, and the shared helper modules (money.py, errors.py) before coding so the implementation matches the intended interface.

rb-0022.title: Reuse existing money helpers instead of reimplementing rounding
rb-0022.description: When a repo already has to_money/round_money utilities, build new monetary functions on top of them rather than writing fresh Decimal logic.
rb-0022.content: Before implementing any amount-handling function, grep for existing money helpers (to_money, round_money, ZERO, CENT) and import them. This keeps rounding policy and float-rejection behavior consistent across modules and avoids subtle mismatches with hidden tests.

rb-0023.title: Validate numeric inputs by converting via Decimal(str(x)) and rejecting bools/non-finite
rb-0023.description: Robust numeric validation converts through str to Decimal, explicitly rejects bool and non-finite values, then range-checks.
rb-0023.content: Pattern: reject isinstance(x, bool) first (since bool is an int subclass), then Decimal(str(x)) inside try/except (InvalidOperation, ValueError), check is_finite(), and finally enforce min/max bounds with a distinct error code. This handles ints, strings, and Decimals uniformly.

rb-0024.title: Match the repo's error convention (BillingError with code) for invalid inputs
rb-0024.description: Sibling modules raise BillingError(code, message) for invalid operations; new validation should follow the same convention.
rb-0024.content: Inspect errors.py and a couple of sibling modules to learn the exception type and code style before writing validation. Use short machine-readable codes (e.g. invalid_rate, rate_out_of_range) and include the offending value as the message, mirroring existing call sites.

rb-0025.title: Reuse project money helpers for currency math
rb-0025.description: When computing monetary values, use the repository's existing to_money/round_money helpers instead of raw Decimal arithmetic.
rb-0025.content: Search for existing money utilities (e.g., round_money, to_money, ZERO) and apply them so rounding and type coercion match project conventions. This keeps new functions consistent with sibling code like invoice totals.

rb-0026.title: Grep for the target symbol and its dependencies before implementing
rb-0026.description: Locate the stub, its dataclass fields, and any existing tests in one pass to infer exact expected behavior.
rb-0026.content: Run grep across source and tests for the function name plus relevant field names (e.g., plan_price, period_days) to find usage examples and expected return types before writing code.

rb-0027.title: Verify edge cases with a quick script after implementing
rb-0027.description: After passing tests, run a small ad-hoc script covering rounding boundaries and type variations to confirm correctness.
rb-0027.content: Exercise cases like non-divisible prices (10/3 -> 3.33), small values, and string-vs-Decimal inputs to catch rounding or coercion bugs that the single provided test may miss.

rb-0028.title: Read CHANGELOG and version for policy thresholds
rb-0028.description: Version-dependent business rules (approval thresholds, limits) are often documented in CHANGELOG/README rather than code, so check them before implementing.
rb-0028.content: When a task involves policy limits or thresholds, grep CHANGELOG.md, README.md and __init__.__version__ for the values and their effective versions. Implement version-aware logic (e.g. threshold 500 before 2.0.0, 1000 since) instead of hardcoding one number.

rb-0029.title: Add optional keyword-only params for new conventions
rb-0029.description: Team conventions like approval requirements can be satisfied without breaking existing callers by adding keyword-only optional parameters.
rb-0029.content: When a review asks for an approval/authorization step, add `*, approved_by=None` to the signature so existing callers keep working, and raise the specified error (e.g. BillingError("approval_required")) only when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given.

rb-0030.title: Mirror existing module conventions for errors and money
rb-0030.description: Reuse the repo's established helpers (to_money/round_money, ZERO, BillingError codes, audit.record) so new functions behave consistently with hidden tests.
rb-0030.content: Before writing a new function, inspect sibling modules for money normalization, error classes and audit logging patterns, and follow them exactly (e.g. round_money(to_money(amount)), BillingError with snake_case codes, audit.record with keyword fields).

rb-0031.title: Match existing module conventions before implementing
rb-0031.description: Reading sibling modules (money, errors, audit, clock, models) revealed the project's helpers and error style, which the accepted implementation reused directly.
rb-0031.content: Before writing a new function, read the modules it will interact with to learn the canonical helpers (e.g. to_money/round_money, BillingError with a code string, audit.record, ensure_utc) and mirror them. Reusing existing utilities avoids float/Decimal bugs and keeps error handling consistent with hidden tests.

rb-0032.title: Validate in the order the spec lists constraints
rb-0032.description: The accepted solution checked positivity, then state, then over-refund, matching the issue's stated rules and the project's error-code conventions.
rb-0032.content: Implement validation checks in the same order the requirements are stated, raising the project's standard error type with a short machine-readable code (e.g. 'non_positive_amount', 'invalid_state', 'refund_exceeds_captured'). Compute the new total from already-refunded plus amount and compare against the captured amount, not the raw payment amount.

rb-0033.title: Reconcile stale memory notes against the changelog
rb-0033.description: A memory note said the approval threshold was 500, but the CHANGELOG raised it to 1000; the agent trusted the changelog.
rb-0033.content: When a remembered constant or policy conflicts with the repository's CHANGELOG/README, prefer the repository source of truth and note the discrepancy. Also avoid adding extra required parameters or behavior (like approval gating) that the issue did not ask for, since hidden tests may call the function with the exact signature specified.
